name: Matbench v0.1 mp_is_metal
description: Predict whether a crystal is a metal (1) or not (0) according to its band gap calculated by density functional theory from its crystal structure (Matbench v0.1 task mp_is_metal, 106113 samples). The evaluation uses the five official folds: for every fold the candidate is called once, in a separate process, with the other four folds and their target values as training data, and must predict the held-out fold within 600 seconds.
contract: fit_predict(train_inputs, train_targets, test_inputs, info) -> list of len(test_inputs) numbers, each exactly 0 or 1 (class labels; any other value is invalid). Every input is a dict with the keys lattice (the three lattice vectors in angstrom, a 3 x 3 list), species (the element symbol of every site) and frac_coords (the fractional coordinates of every site). info has task, input_type, target, unit, fold, n_train and n_test. Score: mean over the five folds of the held-out ROC AUC of the 0/1 labels (which equals the balanced accuracy), maximized.
notes: Leaderboard best 0.952 balanced accuracy (CGCNN v2019), snapshot of matbench.materialsproject.org read 2026-11-03, date unknown.
matbench_mp_is_metal.json.gz from ml.materialsproject.org, folds from the official validation file
Classifies 106,113 Materials Project crystals as metals (1) or non-metals (0) from their structure, scored by ROC AUC on 0/1 labels over the five official folds.
Leaders are graph neural networks and tuned ensembles; the leaderboard snapshot has no date.

The classification score is the ROC AUC of the 0/1 labels, which equals the balanced accuracy: the record is the leaderboard's best balanced accuracy (the page has a second column, probability ROC AUC, that this task does not use).
This task has 106k-133k structures: featurising them is slow, so a candidate must be efficient; the seed uses a cheap feature set.
